videos.title: Uber Eats: how to order food (Russian-language tutorial)
videos.creator: HardReset_info Ukraine
videos.context: Short tutorial with published chapters covering address, cart, delivery and payment. Narration and app language are Russian.

findings.recommendation: Elevate the Uber Eats entry point or add a dedicated persistent bottom tab for food delivery directly inside the primary app home screen to reduce entry steps.
findings.expected_benefit: Decreases the number of navigation taps required to reach food ordering features and increases feature discoverability for users transitioning from rides to delivery services.
findings.title: Nested Uber Eats entry point
findings.description: The user starts on a ride-hailing home screen and must tap a small segmented control at the top to switch to Uber Eats. This requires an extra contextual shift before even browsing restaurants.
findings.visual_evidence: The user's finger taps the small Uber Eats toggle button located at the top right of the main rides interface.
findings.observed_evidence: User navigates from the main rides home screen by tapping the Uber Eats toggle near the header.
findings.interpretation: Embedding food delivery inside a ride app header may obscure the food service for users seeking quick meal delivery.
findings.why_video_matters: Video footage clearly shows the exact navigation path and the small tap target required to access the food ordering section from the default ride view.

suggested_test.hypothesis: If we add a dedicated bottom navigation bar shortcut for food delivery, then users will reach the restaurant listing screen with fewer taps because the entry point is permanently visible.
suggested_test.change: Introduce a bottom navigation tab for Uber Eats alongside rides.

findings.recommendation: Display the restaurant's minimum order requirement directly on the restaurant card or prominently at the top of the menu before items are added, rather than triggering a banner warning in the cart.
findings.expected_benefit: Reduces cart abandonment and back-and-forth navigation between the restaurant menu and cart by setting upfront order value expectations.
findings.title: Hidden minimum order threshold
findings.description: The user adds a single item to the cart and proceeds to checkout, only to be met with a warning banner indicating that the minimum order amount has not been met, forcing them to return to the menu.
findings.visual_evidence: A red warning triangle and text appear in the cart stating 'Измените содержимое корзины, чтобы разместить заказ. До минимальной суммы заказа не хватает 12.00 PLN.'
findings.observed_evidence: User views cart, sees the warning banner about minimum order value, and is forced to tap back to add more items.
findings.interpretation: Discovering minimum order rules only inside the cart creates unnecessary friction and backtracking for users.
findings.why_video_matters: The video captures the exact moment the user encounters the restriction inside the cart view and has to modify their order quantity.

suggested_test.hypothesis: If we display the minimum order amount prominently on the restaurant header, then users will incur fewer backtracks to the menu because they can plan their order size beforehand.
suggested_test.change: Add minimum order requirement text to the top restaurant info banner.
